newsitem.title: USA: Dupont racks up record results.
newsitem.headline: Dupont racks up record results.

text.p: DuPont Co. reported a record first-quarter profit of $1.02 billion, crediting sales of oil and fibers like Lycra for the better-than-expected result, but the chemical giant said results were hurt by the strong dollar.
Net income equalled $1.80 a share, beating Wall Street expectations, and compared with first-quarter 1996 earnings of $879 million, or $1.57 a share.
The Wilmington, Del.-based company's revenues rose 3.7 percent to $11.55 billion from $11.13 billion a year earlier.

"Our results this quarter reflect record petroleum and near-record fibers segment earnings, up 55 percent and 30 percent, respectively, from last year's first quarter," said DuPont President John Krol. "These outstanding results, together with continued control over costs, enabled us to maintain strong earnings growth."
Petroleum sales climbed 15 percent to $5.4 billion from $4.7 billion a year ago, principally due to higher petroleum and natural gas prices.
DuPont's Conoco oil unit said its earnings for the first quarter jumped 55 percent to $331 million vs. year earlier earnings of $214 million.
Sales of chemicals and specialities rose 3 percent to $5.9 billion after adjustments for divestitures or joint ventures.
Chemicals and specialities volumes were up 7 percent, rising 6 percent in the United States, 5 percent in Europe, and in other regions combined 13 percent.
DuPont stock dropped $1.50 to $106.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
